html:
Susquehanna marks the Susquehannock, an Iroquoian-speaking people of the lower Susquehanna River valley in what is now Pennsylvania and Maryland. They lived in large palisaded towns and farmed maize, beans and squash.

John Smith met them in 1608 and described them as tall and well armed. They traded furs with the Swedes, Dutch and English and were long at war with the Haudenosaunee to the north. By the 1670s war and disease had broken them, and Maryland and Virginia turned against them too. The survivors, called Conestoga, lived in a small village in Pennsylvania until 1763, when the vigilantes known as the Paxton Boys killed the last of them. See Susquehannock and their neighbours the Conoy.
